## 非農強勁推升升息機率，年薪資增速卻放慢

美國聘僱超過彭博調查所有預估，收回部分週四前端漲幅，也讓聯準會更有空間處理通膨。8月非農增加16.2萬，向上修正更消除了原先公布的7月減員。9月升息機率由約50%升至60%，2年期殖利率一度上升8個基點，收盤漲幅縮至3個基點、報4.37%。

薪資則讓投資人不必追著拋售。時薪月增0.3%，年增率卻降至3.1%，為2021年以來最低。10年期殖利率升1個基點至4.78%，與實質殖利率升至2.43%的幅度相同，損益兩平通膨率維持2.35%。30年期反而降1個基點至5.24%，使2s30s收窄4個基點至87個基點。就業改善減少升息的一項顧慮，卻未顯示長期通膨補償再度加速。

美國投資級與高收益利差近乎不變，強勢貨幣新興市場債利差小幅收窄，VIX收14.53。資金仍可取得，條件卻更分歧：高評等科技債開始吸引相對價值買盤，SoftBank用大型零售債接觸日本家庭，Air Baltic則提出利率25%的超優先過橋融資，不參與者順位將後退。塞內加爾稍晚降評、印尼國企延遲付款，也與廣泛信用指數的平靜形成對比。

下週通膨因而更重要。聘僱強勁，仍可以與Waller認為足以支持等待的價格降溫並存。燃料成本是持續風險；週五收盤後的週末油輪攻擊，又讓亞洲新一週無法放下這項顧慮。

## 聘僱改善擴及更多企業，年薪資增長未加速

非農增加16.2萬，對比約5.5萬預估及過去12個月平均3.1萬。6月由2萬上修至3.1萬，7月由減2.3萬改為增2.1萬，合計上修5.5萬。民間企業增12.7萬、前期7.1萬，政府增3.5萬、前期減5萬。原先看似7月收縮，改成持續但不均勻的增長。

家庭調查也轉強。就業增加56.9萬、勞動力增加68.3萬，失業率維持4.1%；參與率由61.4%升至61.6%，近一年首次增加，就業人口比由58.9%升至59.1%。參與率改善來自較年輕與較年長者，主要工作年齡仍為83.4%。

餐旅與學校聘僱貢獻很大。餐飲場所增加5.9萬，過去12個月平均僅1.2萬；地方政府教育增4.2萬，大致逆轉7月下滑，但2025年1月以來淨變化很小。製造增1.6萬、前期1.4萬，機械與金屬製品各增6,000，使2025年12月以來累增5.8萬；建築增2.2萬。民間產業擴散指數由52.8升至55.6，製造由52.1升至61.1，顯示改善不只集中於增聘最大的產業。

其他服務較弱。醫療增加1.3萬，低於平均3.2萬，其中居家照護增1.1萬、醫院8,000。資訊減2.3萬，包括運算基礎設施、資料處理與代管減8,000，出版7,000，廣播及內容供應5,000；金融減1.1萬。建築與製造增加、資訊減員，與建設及使用AI可能帶來不同影響相符，但報告無法證明每個變化都由科技造成。

平均時薪達$37.75，月增0.3%、年增3.1%；生產與非主管時薪也增0.3%至$32.53。民間每週工時增0.1小時至34.4，兩年多最高；製造增0.1至40.5，加班維持3.1，生產與非主管工時維持33.8。非自願兼職減41.4萬至440萬，但長期失業仍有190萬、占失業者27.0%，另有570萬未在勞動力中但想工作。人數及工時增加，使家庭總收入即使在薪資增速放慢時仍可成長。

較早的建築支出資料，卻不支持將聘僱增加視為全面投資熱潮。7月名目支出連續第12個月年減，較2025年2月高峰低近5%，為三年多最弱水準，資料中心只占3.5%。PPG Macro的Patrick Perret-Green估計，扣除資料中心後的收縮速度，為2006年房市繁榮結束以來最快；製造建築支出年減約21%。KPMG的Yelena Maleyev也指出，扣除資料中心及其電力基礎設施後，非住宅建築正在收縮。期間雖早於8月聘僱，仍顯示投資高度集中。

克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack週五認為，數據與轄區回報支持採取行動，因為政策未充分抑制活動。這名7月主張升息的委員引用俄亥俄州製造商案例：多項投入價格兩位數上漲，企業甚至要求提高利率。她在非農後仍堅定，另一端則是Waller有條件等待的立場。交換市場反映年底前緊縮35個基點，也有SOFR選擇權部位押注全年不再升息，分歧仍在。

川普要求降息，並威脅若聯準會不配合，將中止與對美順差國的貿易。此舉可能面臨法律挑戰，也沒有清楚路徑能降低借款成本。Kevin Hassett則表示就業報告支持維持利率，同時承認聯準會獨立。兩者都是政治立場，不會直接改變委員會票數。

## 買方尋找政府債以外收益，科技債價值浮現

摩根大通指出，美國銀行貸款持續增加，8月投資級淨發債也提高，儘管美債流動性明顯惡化，股指期貨與公司債ETF未見相同壓力。廣泛利差穩定之下，Schwab的Collin Martin觀察到CCC擴大，BB與B卻收窄。

挪威主權基金提議，將$2.3兆投資組合中債券配置的政府證券比重，由70%降至50%。彭博估算可能代表美債減少約$750億、日債增加約$200億，不是已完成交易或出售時程。NAB的Kenneth Crompton認為，既有流動性資產已足夠，可轉向其他債券風險溢價。Bessent說若轉投房屋機構債等美國資產，可能有正面效果，但未確定挪威最終選擇。政府長債需求可能減少，不等於退出美國市場。

穩定幣增長也不如額外短券買盤的期待。加密交易轉弱，使USDT上半年縮近$30億至約$1,840億，USDC也縮相近金額至約$720億。Tether與Circle分別持有約$1,340億及$630億美債與政府債支持的附買回資產。準備資產規模不小，但代幣增長放慢，對約$7兆短券市場的新增需求便較有限。

支付業務可能提供另一條成長路徑。7月穩定幣卡片支付首度突破$10億，McKinsey估計年度支付約$3,900億，主要為企業間交易。Tether表示，支付抵銷部分交易需求下滑。不過，同一代幣重複使用不需要等額增加準備資產，支付周轉不能直接等同美債需求。

DoubleLine的Robert Cohen開始在密集發行的科技債看到價值。投資級科技利差比大盤高近10個基點；Alphabet的8月10年期新券週五約81個基點，2月券則在發行後擴大約15個基點至76。廣泛指數近80，平均評等卻低於Alphabet的AA+及Amazon的AA。強健借款人提供更多收益補償，也可能迫使較弱企業及資料中心發行人提高條件。

供給仍在增加。Anthropic正由Morgan Stanley主導，把循環額度擴至$150億，尚在定案。Societe Generale研究1,500家上市非金融企業發現，最大AI支出者增募股債、放慢庫藏股；即使投資上升，整體企業現金仍再創高點。

Volkswagen方向不同。董事會一致支持Oliver Blume再裁5萬人、減少車型及縮小工業布局，但四座德國工廠去留未定，股價週五漲6.5%。另一則收盤後更新是鴻海週一清晨公布月營收增52%，由伺服器帶動；這支持AI投資集中的觀察，不能用來解釋週五利率。

SoftBank為¥1兆、約$63億七年期零售債定價，接近4.3%至4.9%指引上緣，對比今年日圓零售公司債平均票息2.3%。計入本次，截至9月4日發行已達¥2.88兆，超過所有歷年全年。SoftBank在本地評等屬投資級，主要國際機構卻屬投機級；高票息吸引家庭，也補償信用風險。

印度REC徵求至多₹50億、約$5,300萬代幣化債券投標，2028年5月到期，可能是印度首筆。投資人必須使用央行數位貨幣。自動化債務服務與減少交割中介，可能拓展規模約GDP 17%的公司債市場，但尚非完成發行或次級流動性改善的證明。

Pimco的Christian Stracke警告，部分基金擔保債務憑證及重大風險移轉，對內含槓桿補償不足。CFO將基金股權轉成有評等債務，常由保險公司持有；SRT則移轉銀行貸款風險。他指出的是局部錯價，不是系統危機，並提到整體槓桿低於金融危機前。

部分機構也重新加黃金。Amundi、Pictet、Robeco與Fidelity International在先前減持後回補；涵蓋管理$27兆資產機構的訪談，顯示重新買入或維持偏多。Robeco引用第2季央行買入289噸，Amundi則等待聯準會更明朗，再決定是否加碼8月買入部位。這些中期選擇與黃金週五因非農而下跌可以並存。

## 燃油壓力讓航空過橋融資代價高昂

WTI收$91.48、布蘭特$96.28。週四美國汽油均價每加侖$4.15，創9月紀錄，高於7月4日$3.80；柴油達紀錄$5.85。墨西哥灣沿岸航空燃油本週也升至數月高點。

高收益航空利差接近400個基點，超過1月兩倍。惠譽的Joseph Rohlena指出燃油約占成本20%。Delta與JetBlue第2季每可用座位英里收入均年增11%，但高端及國際旅客給United與Delta更大保障，小型國內業者的價格敏感客群較難承受漲價。

借款成本已明顯不同於戰前。United在2月募集$20億，其中五年期$10億、5.375%；Alaska在5月以幾乎相同BB評等募集五年$5億，殖利率6.5%。借款人與時間不同，不能視為單獨衡量燃油衝擊的對照；Barings的Chad Campbell仍預期戰爭拖長將使新融資需要更多補償。

JetBlue的9.875%會員忠誠計畫支持債、2031年到期，週四回到約84美分，接近7月低點，遠低於2月104。財報會後回升未能維持，這批債占高收益航空指數12%。公司表示將專注營收及可控成本；會員計畫擔保提供特定請求權，仍不能消除營運流動性疑慮。

Air Baltic提出由Polus Capital Management與Klirmark Capital提供至多€2.57億、約$2.99億臨時融資，同時協商重整。Polus認購至少一半超優先債，兩家基金承諾補足未認購餘額。年息25%，基金另取得約€3,000萬超優先債作費用。這家88%國有航空公司已獲拉脫維亞政府€3,000萬短期貸款。

過橋債2027年2月26日到期，首批可得€1.8億，第二筆則須符合與利害關係人達成重整協議等條件，預計重整完成時再融資。因此最高金額不是全部立即可用，也不是無條件的長期營運資金。

提供新資金者可將部分2029年債換成較高順位，Klirmark另有私下升順位交換。不參與者將落在新超優先債及參與者之後。拉脫維亞持有約13%既有債，可選擇出資，國會授權購買至多€3,000萬新券。國有身分並未阻止不參與債權人可能被降至較後順位。

葡萄牙則在Lufthansa與Air France-KLM對TAP的出價總值相近後，展開另一輪協商。擬售至多49.9%，其中44.9%給策略投資人、至多5%給員工，尚未完成處分或取得款項。

Bessent在週五播出的訪談稱，伊朗衝突結束後油價可能降至$50或$40，但沒有時間表。週末未帶來立即緩解：美軍表示，兩艘美國軍艦遭攻擊後，擊中三艘伊朗原油輪；伊朗宣稱攻擊三艘油輪及其他美國相關船隻，起初未確認命中。布蘭特週一早盤小升。這些事件影響接下來的融資前景，不是週五收盤成因。

## 塞內加爾降評，重整涵蓋哪些債權再成焦點

標普週五稍晚將塞內加爾由CCC+降至CC、展望負向，認為外幣商業債極可能困境交換或違約，債權人會在本金、利息或時間上受損。更重要的是，標普質疑龐大國內債務能否排除，挑戰政府保護西非法郎義務的說法。

花旗估計，塞內加爾占BOAD貸款約17%、Afreximbank不到4%、Ecobank約6%、Africa Finance Corp.約8%，後者未含結構型主權流動性交易。Nikola Apostolov列出的不利風險包括IMF延後批准、拖欠多邊機構、優先債權地位被挑戰，以及法郎債納入。$22億IMF計畫仍須董事會同意；花旗基本情境則容許BOAD與Afreximbank利差暫時落後，未預期基本信用大幅惡化。

債務主管Alioune Diouf說會繼續償付所有債務。倫敦下午2:22，2031年美元債跌0.21美分至50.83，2048年債漲0.14至50.70，均早於降評，不是市場對降評的反應。另一端，薩爾瓦多在與IMF就延伸基金安排審查達成工作人員層級協議後，債券上漲。

印尼Adhi Karya在重整中未支付前週到期利息約Rp608億、$340萬。四家大型國有建商年底合計債務近Rp118兆，接近Danantara今年預計上繳政府的Rp120兆，主要來自國企股利。救助需求與繳庫、新投資爭奪同一批資金。

Danantara管理逾800家國企，希望縮至約200家。官方估值$9,000億資產不等於可立即動用現金，融資仍靠股利及借款。CreditSights認為Adhi規模大、較可能獲支持；Alvarez & Marsal的Alessandro Gazzini則認為問題集中建築，並非整體國企。不過，Pos Indonesia在7月延遲支付Rp241億伊斯蘭債息後，也披露2023至2025年Rp9兆會計調整；它已補付並加補償，與Adhi未解決的延遲不同。

重整可能迫使銀行延長到期、承擔損失，並留存壓力資產更久。同批銀行也服務退出海外債市的民企：Jababeka在6月用Bank Mandiri長期貸款償還$1.859億美元債，Modernland則為明年約$2.745億到期債尋求五年內第三次重整。支持可避免驟然倒閉，仍會占用銀行能力。

巴西Bruno Moretti表示，Lula若再任，可透過放慢強制支出增長，四年改善初級收支約GDP 2個百分點。2027提案目標R$186億、$37億或GDP 0.13%盈餘，對比今年預計0.4%赤字，最終目標1.5%盈餘。仍須總統審查，Moretti又排除讓退休金增速低於最低工資，限制選項。

預算另編R$979億公共基金補貼貸款，批評者認為可能在初級收支與支出限制之外增加債務。Moretti表示撥款漸進，不會造成通膨需求衝擊。總債務已達GDP 82.5%，排除利息及這些放款的初級目標，仍不是完整融資計畫。

另一項收盤後消息是，週一清晨至少八家中國大型銀行與保險公司尋求CN¥3,600億、約$536億新資本，財政部提供逾80%，涉及CN¥3,000億、$447億特別債，以減輕利差壓力、支持放貸並提列壞帳準備。這是已宣布支持，並非全部完成增資，也不是週五美國收盤成因。

## 有些央行能降息，有些仍須等待通膨

哈薩克週五降息50個基點至16.25%，連續第三次，8月通膨已放慢至9.8%。六名經濟學家預期降25個基點，兩人估降至16%，一人估不變。官員維持今年9%至11%通膨預測，卻將明年由5.5%至7.5%調高至6.5%至8.5%，警告剩餘寬鬆空間有限。

油收入提高之下，堅戈今年升近11%、上次決策以來約4%。ING的Dmitry Dolgin將匯率視為主要剩餘降通膨來源，預期年底利率可能在16%至16.25%觸底。但石油基金擬提領額從今年T2.77兆升至2027年T4.4兆、約$96億，增加財政變數。

捷克通膨1.9%符合市場與央行預測，服務由4.7%降至4.5%。食品效果及電力措施影響消退，可能在2027年初推升通膨，能源與較大預算赤字也有風險。BlackRock及Societe Generale仍看好維持利率；後者預期3.75%，市場卻反映年底前升25個基點、2027年中累計100個基點。

紐西蘭Karen Silk進一步說明，預測路徑偏向12月而非10月再升。週五交換市場反映10月到3%的機率31%，12月則完全反映。她是六名委員中四名強調上行風險者之一，包括中東中斷、企業定價能力恢復，以及保險、電力、土地稅；但未因此選擇不同決策，也不需投票。

歐洲央行預期首次升息之後仍有分歧。彭博調查大致認為2.5%將維持至2027年，市場卻反映到年中約再升三次。JPMorgan、Societe Generale及BNP Paribas已轉向預測12月額外一次。Isabel Schnabel強調要在需要更激烈行動前防止第二輪效應，Martin Kocher則預期未來數月更清楚；目前相關證據仍有限。

管理£2,530億的Aviva Investors本週買入10年英債。Steve Ryder認為債息上升會限制政府支出，資產交換利差大致穩定，也顯示拋售較來自通膨與政策，而非新一輪供給恐慌。週五10年殖利率約5.15%。以先前已報導的£120億財政緩衝損失為背景，他預期政府會平衡調整、貨幣最終轉鬆，並將前端部位轉至兩年後起算的一年期利率，降低眼前升息敏感度。

摩根大通估計，開發中國家通膨3.8%，約2022年三分之一，政策緩衝比四年前多約1個百分點。本幣新興債今年回報逾3%，對比美債與歐洲同業虧損0.6%。起始利率提供選擇性配置理由，不是對所有財政品質的背書。

週五收盤後，ARD週日預測AfD在薩克森－安哈特得票44%，超過前次兩倍，CDU為17.5%。歐元亞洲早盤近乎不變。政治轉向幅度增加不確定性，但本身不直接改變德國財政政策，也不能解釋週五價格。

## 下週通膨、標售與債權人表決接連登場

9月10日紐約上午8:30公布PPI，整體與核心均估月增0.3%；11日同時公布CPI，整體估0.4%、前期0.1%，核心0.2%，核心年增由2.5%降至2.4%。若基礎通膨受控，即使聘僱強，9月16日聯準會仍有維持利率理由；若廣泛加速，則有利鷹派。歐洲央行10日升至2.5%已廣受預期，後續指引更重要。

美國財政部9日公布10日擴大買回細節，承諾至少為原先$20億上限兩倍，不是市場猜測的更高倍數。3年、10年與30年標售分別在8、9、10日。企業供給與潛在機構調整同時爭取資金，買盤及流動性改善程度將顯示官方支持是否有效。

Air Baltic債權人11日表決臨時融資與順位變更，Adhi Karya也安排當日就欠息開會；塞內加爾承諾持續償債，將面對13日2048年境外債付款。實際支付與批准可釐清眼前現金及法律地位，仍不消除最終重整損失。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Stronger payrolls revive hike odds, but wages slow

US hiring beat every estimate in Bloomberg's survey, reversing part of Thursday's front-end rally and giving the Federal Reserve more room to confront inflation. August payrolls rose 162,000, with upward revisions removing July's reported decline. September hike odds rose from about 50% to 60%. The 2-year yield initially gained as much as 8 basis points before closing 3 higher at 4.37%.

Wages offered a reason not to chase the selloff. Annual earnings growth slowed to 3.1%, the weakest since 2021, despite a 0.3% monthly increase. The 10-year yield rose 1 basis point to 4.78%, matching a real-yield increase to 2.43%, while breakevens held at 2.35%. The 30-year fell 1 basis point to 5.24%, narrowing 2s30s by 4 to 87 basis points. Better employment reduced one obstacle to tightening without showing a fresh acceleration in long-term inflation compensation.

US IG and HY spreads barely changed, hard-currency EM tightened modestly and VIX closed at 14.53. Financing remained available, but increasingly on different terms: highly rated technology debt drew relative-value interest, SoftBank reached Japanese households with a large retail sale, and Air Baltic proposed a 25% super-senior bridge that would subordinate nonparticipants. Senegal's late downgrade and Indonesian state-enterprise payment problems also stood apart from calm broad credit indices.

Next week's inflation data now carry more weight. Strong hiring can coexist with the moderation Christopher Waller said would justify waiting. Persistent fuel costs remain a threat, while weekend tanker attacks—after Friday's close—kept that threat alive heading into the Asian week.

## Hiring improves across more employers without faster annual pay growth

Payrolls increased 162,000 against expectations near 55,000 and a prior 12-month average of 31,000. June was revised from 20,000 to 31,000 and July from −23,000 to +21,000, a combined upward revision of 55,000. Private employers added 127,000 after 71,000; government added 35,000 after losing 50,000. The report replaced an apparent July contraction with a run of uneven gains.

The household survey strengthened too. Employment rose 569,000 and the labor force 683,000, leaving unemployment at 4.1%. Participation increased to 61.6% from 61.4%, its first gain in almost a year, and the employment-population ratio to 59.1% from 58.9%. Younger and older workers drove participation; the prime-age rate stayed at 83.4%.

Hospitality and school payrolls made large contributions. Food services and drinking places added 59,000 versus a 12-month average of 12,000. Local-government education added 42,000, largely reversing July with little net change since January 2025. Manufacturing gained 16,000 after 14,000, including 6,000 each in machinery and fabricated metals, bringing its increase since December 2025 to 58,000. Construction added 22,000. Private-industry diffusion rose to 55.6 from 52.8 and manufacturing diffusion to 61.1 from 52.1, showing wider improvement beyond the largest hiring sectors.

Other services lagged. Health care added 13,000 against its 32,000 average, including 11,000 in home care and 8,000 in hospitals. Information lost 23,000: computing infrastructure, data processing and hosting fell 8,000, publishing 7,000 and broadcasting/content providers 5,000. Financial activities lost 11,000. Construction and manufacturing strength alongside information-sector cuts is consistent with differing effects from building and using AI, although the report does not establish that technology caused each change.

Average hourly earnings reached $37.75, up 0.3% monthly and 3.1% annually. Production and nonsupervisory pay also rose 0.3%, to $32.53. The private workweek gained 0.1 hour to 34.4, its highest in over two years; manufacturing rose 0.1 to 40.5, with overtime unchanged at 3.1. Production and nonsupervisory hours stayed at 33.8. Involuntary part-time work fell 414,000 to 4.4 million, though long-term unemployment remained 1.9 million, or 27.0% of the unemployed, and 5.7 million outside the labor force wanted work. More workers and hours can sustain household income even with slower wage growth.

Earlier construction spending data caution against treating the hiring gain as a broad investment boom. July nominal spending recorded its 12th consecutive month of year-over-year decline, almost 5% below February 2025's peak and the weakest pace in over three years. Data centers were only 3.5% of spending. PPG Macro's Patrick Perret-Green estimated that excluding them left construction contracting fastest since the end of the 2006 housing boom; manufacturing construction fell about 21% annually. KPMG's Yelena Maleyev also found nonresidential contraction outside data centers and their power infrastructure. These measures precede August hiring but reveal how concentrated investment remains.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said Friday that data and district reports warranted action because policy was not sufficiently restraining activity. The July dissenter cited an Ohio manufacturer reporting double-digit input-price increases and asking for higher rates. Her view remained forceful after payrolls, while Waller's conditional willingness to hold remained the counterweight. Swaps priced 35 basis points of tightening by year-end; a SOFR-options position targeting no increase illustrated the continuing disagreement.

Donald Trump demanded lower rates and threatened to halt trade with surplus countries if the Fed did not comply. Such action would likely face a legal challenge, with no clear route to lower borrowing costs. Kevin Hassett instead said the jobs report supported a hold while acknowledging Fed independence. Neither political preference changes the committee's votes.

## Buyers find alternatives to government debt and cheaper technology credit

JPMorgan reported growing US bank lending and higher net IG issuance in August despite sharply worse Treasury liquidity. Stock-index futures and corporate-bond ETFs showed little comparable stress. Beneath stable aggregate spreads, Schwab's Collin Martin noted CCC widening while BB and B tightened.

Norway's sovereign fund proposed reducing government securities from 70% to 50% of the bond allocation in its $2.3 trillion portfolio. Bloomberg calculations imply about $75 billion less in Treasuries and potentially $20 billion more in JGBs, not completed transactions or a sale timetable. NAB's Kenneth Crompton saw sufficient existing liquidity holdings allowing more exposure to other bond risk premiums. Scott Bessent said a move into other US assets, including agency housing debt, could be constructive, without establishing Norway's eventual choices. The proposal could reduce government-duration demand without representing an exit from US markets.

Stablecoin growth has also disappointed hopes for additional bill buying. USDT shrank nearly $3 billion in the first half to about $184 billion, and USDC by a similar amount to roughly $72 billion as crypto trading weakened. Tether and Circle reported about $134 billion and $63 billion in Treasuries and government-backed reverse repos. Their reserves matter, but slower token growth offers less incremental demand to the roughly $7 trillion bill market.

Payments could provide a different source of expansion. Stablecoin card payments exceeded $1 billion in July for the first time, while McKinsey estimated annual payments near $390 billion, mostly business-to-business. Tether said payments offset some trading weakness. Repeated use of existing tokens, however, does not require matching reserve creation; payment turnover cannot be treated as an equal increase in Treasury demand.

DoubleLine's Robert Cohen found better value in heavily issued technology debt. IG technology spreads were nearly 10 basis points above the broad market. Alphabet's August 10-year issue traded near 81 basis points Friday; its February issue around 76 after widening about 15 since sale. The broad index was near 80 despite a lower average rating than Alphabet's AA+ and Amazon's AA. Better compensation from strong borrowers could force riskier companies and data-center issuers to offer more.

Supply is still growing. Anthropic was finalizing an expansion of its revolving facility to $15 billion, led by Morgan Stanley. Societe Generale's study of 1,500 listed nonfinancial companies found the largest AI spenders raising debt and equity while moderating buybacks; aggregate corporate cash again reached records despite higher investment.

Volkswagen is moving in another direction. Its board unanimously backed Oliver Blume's plan for 50,000 additional job cuts, fewer models and a smaller footprint, though four German plants' future remained unresolved. Shares rose 6.5% Friday. In a later update, Hon Hai reported a 52% monthly sales increase driven by servers early Monday. That post-close evidence reinforces AI investment concentration but did not cause Friday's rates move.

SoftBank priced a ¥1 trillion, or $6.3 billion, seven-year retail bond at the upper end of its 4.3%–4.9% guidance. This year's average yen retail corporate coupon was 2.3%. The sale brought issuance to ¥2.88 trillion by September 4, above every previous full-year total. SoftBank carries domestic investment-grade but major global speculative-grade ratings; the higher coupon attracts households while compensating credit risk.

India's REC sought bids for up to ₹5 billion, or $53 million, of tokenized notes due May 2028, potentially the country's first. Investors must use RBI digital currency. Automated servicing and fewer settlement intermediaries could broaden a corporate market around 17% of GDP, but the proposal is not a completed sale or proof of better secondary liquidity.

Pimco's Christian Stracke warned that some collateralized fund obligations and significant risk transfers underpay investors for embedded leverage. CFOs turn fund-equity interests into rated debt, often for insurers; SRTs transfer bank loan risk. He identified pockets of mispricing rather than a systemic crisis, noting leverage below pre-financial-crisis levels.

Some allocators are adding gold as well. Amundi, Pictet, Robeco and Fidelity International rebuilt positions after earlier reductions; interviews covering managers of $27 trillion found renewed buying or continued bullish allocations. Robeco cited Q2 central-bank purchases of 289 tons. Amundi awaited greater Fed clarity before adding to August purchases. These medium-term choices coexist with gold's immediate Friday decline after payrolls.

## Fuel pressure puts a high price on airline bridge financing

WTI closed at $91.48 and Brent $96.28. US gasoline averaged $4.15 a gallon Thursday, a September record versus $3.80 on July 4, while diesel reached a record $5.85. Gulf Coast jet fuel hit its highest in months during the week.

High-yield airline spreads were near 400 basis points, more than twice January's level. Fitch's Joseph Rohlena put fuel near 20% of costs. Delta and JetBlue each increased Q2 revenue per available seat mile 11% annually, but premium and international demand give United and Delta more protection than smaller domestic carriers serving price-sensitive passengers.

Borrowing costs already differ sharply from prewar levels. United raised $2 billion in February, including $1 billion for five years at 5.375%. Alaska's $500 million five-year May issue yielded 6.5% at an almost identical BB rating. These are different borrowers and dates, not a controlled fuel-cost comparison; Barings' Chad Campbell nevertheless expected more compensation for new funding as the war persisted.

JetBlue's 9.875% loyalty-backed 2031 notes returned to about 84 cents Thursday, near July's low and far below February's 104. They had failed to sustain an earnings-call recovery and represent 12% of the HY airline index. The airline said it was concentrating on revenue and controllable costs. Loyalty collateral gives a specific claim but does not remove concern about operating liquidity.

Air Baltic proposed up to €257 million, or $299 million, of interim financing from Polus Capital Management and Klirmark Capital while negotiating a restructuring. Polus would subscribe to at least half the super-senior notes, with both funds backstopping the unsubscribed balance. Interest would be 25%, and the funds would receive roughly €30 million of additional super-senior debt in fees. The 88%-state-owned airline already received a €30 million short-term Latvian government loan.

The bridge matures February 26, 2027. Initial proceeds would be €180 million; a second installment requires, among other conditions, stakeholder agreement on restructuring. The debt is intended to be refinanced when the restructuring closes, so the maximum amount is neither immediate cash nor an unconditional runway.

New-money participants could exchange some 2029 bonds into higher-ranking debt, and Klirmark would receive a private uptier exchange. Nonparticipants would rank behind both new super-senior creditors and participating holders. Latvia owns about 13% of existing bonds and may provide new money; parliament authorized up to €30 million of purchases. State ownership has not prevented proposed subordination of creditors that decline to participate.

Portugal instead opened another negotiating round with Lufthansa and Air France-KLM over TAP after offers were close in total value. The planned sale is up to 49.9%: 44.9% for a strategic investor and up to 5% for employees. No disposal or proceeds are yet complete.

Bessent said in an interview aired Friday that oil could fall to $50 or $40 after the Iran conflict, without a timeframe. Weekend events offered no immediate relief: the US military said it hit three Iranian crude tankers following attacks on two US warships. Iran claimed attacks on three tankers and other US-linked ships, initially without confirming hits. Brent edged higher early Monday. These later events affect the coming week's funding outlook, not Friday's completed prices.

## Senegal's downgrade puts the creditor perimeter back in focus

S&P cut Senegal to CC from CCC+ late Friday, with a negative outlook, judging a distressed exchange or default on foreign-currency commercial debt extremely likely. It expects creditors to receive less through principal, interest or timing. It also questioned whether the large domestic debt stock could remain excluded, challenging the government's stated protection of CFA-franc obligations.

Citi put Senegal at about 17% of BOAD's loan book, under 4% of Afreximbank's, roughly 6% of Ecobank's and about 8% of Africa Finance Corp.'s, excluding AFC structured sovereign liquidity transactions. Nikola Apostolov highlighted delayed IMF approval, missed multilateral payments, challenges to preferred-creditor status and inclusion of CFA debt as adverse risks. The $2.2 billion IMF program still requires board approval. Citi's base case allows temporary BOAD and Afreximbank spread underperformance without material fundamental damage.

Debt director Alioune Diouf said all debt would continue to be serviced. At 2:22 p.m. London, the 2031 dollar bond fell 0.21 cents to 50.83 and the 2048 rose 0.14 to 50.70. Those prices preceded the downgrade and were not a response to it. Elsewhere, El Salvador bonds rallied after an IMF staff-level agreement on extended-fund-facility reviews.

Indonesia's Adhi Karya missed about Rp60.8 billion, or $3.4 million, of interest due the previous week during restructuring. Four large state builders had nearly Rp118 trillion of combined debt at year-end, close to Danantara's expected Rp120 trillion remittance to government this year, mainly from state-company dividends. Rescue needs compete with both remittances and new investment.

Danantara manages over 800 state enterprises and aims to reduce them to about 200. Its officially valued $900 billion asset base is not a ready cash pool: funding relies on dividends and borrowing. CreditSights saw Adhi's size supporting the likelihood of assistance; Alvarez & Marsal's Alessandro Gazzini considered problems concentrated in construction rather than system-wide. Pos Indonesia nevertheless disclosed Rp9 trillion of accounting adjustments for 2023–25 after missing a Rp24.1 billion sukuk coupon in July. It later paid with extra compensation, unlike Adhi's unresolved delay.

Restructurings may require banks to extend maturities, take losses and retain stressed assets longer. The same lenders serve private companies leaving offshore markets: Jababeka used long-term Bank Mandiri funding to repay $185.9 million of dollar notes in June, while Modernland seeks its third restructuring in five years for about $274.5 million due next year. Support can prevent abrupt failure while still using bank capacity.

Brazil's Bruno Moretti said another Lula term could improve the primary balance by about 2 percentage points of GDP over four years through slower mandatory-spending growth. The 2027 proposal targets R$18.6 billion, or $3.7 billion and 0.13% of GDP, in surplus versus a projected 0.4% deficit this year; the eventual target is 1.5% surplus. Presidential review is pending, and Moretti ruled out pension growth below the minimum wage, limiting options.

The budget also allocates R$97.9 billion to subsidized public-fund lending, which critics say can add debt outside primary and spending limits. Moretti said disbursement would be gradual and would not create an inflationary demand shock. With gross debt at 82.5% of GDP, a primary target excluding interest and these lending programs is not a complete financing plan.

In a separate post-close development, at least eight major Chinese banks and insurers sought CN¥360 billion, or $53.6 billion, of fresh capital by early Monday. The finance ministry would provide over 80%, involving CN¥300 billion, or $44.7 billion, of special bonds to relieve margin pressure, support lending and fund bad-loan provisions. This is announced support, not a completed recapitalization or a cause of Friday's US close.

## Inflation gives some central banks room to ease, others reason to wait

Kazakhstan cut 50 basis points to 16.25% Friday, its third reduction, after August inflation slowed to 9.8%. Six surveyed economists expected 25 basis points, two a move to 16% and one no change. Officials kept 2026 inflation at 9%–11% but raised next year's range to 6.5%–8.5% from 5.5%–7.5%, warning that remaining easing room was limited.

The tenge gained nearly 11% this year and about 4% since the previous decision as oil revenue strengthened. ING's Dmitry Dolgin saw the currency as the main remaining disinflation source and rates potentially bottoming at 16%–16.25% by year-end. Planned oil-fund withdrawals rise to T4.4 trillion, or $9.6 billion, in 2027 from T2.77 trillion, adding a fiscal complication.

Czech inflation reached 1.9%, matching both the survey and central-bank forecasts, while services slowed to 4.5% from 4.7%. Food effects and the fading impact of electricity measures could lift inflation in early 2027, alongside energy and a larger prospective deficit. BlackRock and Societe Generale nevertheless see scope to hold. SocGen expects 3.75%, against markets pricing 25 basis points by year-end and 100 cumulatively by mid-2027.

RBNZ's Karen Silk clarified that its projected path favored another increase in December rather than October. Friday swaps assigned 31% odds to 3% in October and fully priced it by December. She was among four of six committee members emphasizing upside risks from Middle East disruption, firms' recovering pricing power, insurance, electricity and land taxes. Those concerns did not produce a different preferred decision or require a vote.

ECB forecasts remain divided after the expected initial hike. A Bloomberg survey broadly saw 2.5% through 2027, while market pricing extended to roughly three further increases by midyear. JPMorgan, Societe Generale and BNP Paribas had moved toward an additional December hike. Isabel Schnabel stressed preventing second-round effects before stronger action became necessary; Martin Kocher expected more clarity over coming months. Evidence of those effects remained limited.

Aviva Investors, managing £253 billion, bought 10-year gilts during the week. Steve Ryder argued that higher debt service would constrain spending, while broadly stable asset-swap spreads suggested inflation and policy—not newly intensified supply concerns—drove the selloff. Ten-year yields were around 5.15% Friday. With the previously reported £12 billion fiscal-buffer loss as context, he expected a balanced budget response and eventual easing, and shifted front-end exposure to the two-year-forward one-year rate to reduce immediate-hike sensitivity.

JPMorgan estimated developing-country inflation at 3.8%, roughly one-third of 2022's level, with about 1 percentage point more policy cushion than four years ago. Local-currency EM bonds returned over 3% this year against 0.6% losses for Treasuries and European peers. Those starting rates support selective demand, not a blanket judgment about fiscal quality.

After Friday's close, ARD's Sunday projection gave AfD 44% in Saxony-Anhalt, more than twice its prior support, versus CDU's 17.5%. The euro was little changed early in Asia. The scale adds political uncertainty but does not itself change German fiscal policy or explain Friday's bond prices.

## Inflation, auctions and creditor votes fill next week's calendar

US PPI is due September 10 at 8:30 a.m. ET, with headline and core each expected at 0.3% monthly. CPI follows September 11 at the same time: headline consensus is 0.4% after 0.1%, core 0.2%, and annual core 2.4% from 2.5%. Contained underlying inflation would preserve a September 16 Fed hold argument despite stronger hiring; broader acceleration would favor the hawks. The ECB's September 10 move to 2.5% is widely expected, leaving guidance on subsequent increases more important.

Treasury announces expanded buyback details September 9 for September 10. The commitment is at least twice the prior $2 billion maximum, not the larger multiples under speculation. Three-, 10- and 30-year auctions fall September 8, 9 and 10. Demand and liquidity improvement will show whether the support helps as corporate supply and prospective institutional reallocations compete for buyers.

Air Baltic holders vote September 11 on interim funding and priority changes; Adhi Karya is arranging a meeting that day over its missed interest. Senegal's stated commitment to service debt faces the September 13 payment on its 2048 foreign bond. Actual payment and approvals would clarify immediate cash and legal positions without removing eventual restructuring losses.

section_summaries.summary: Upward revisions, wider hiring and improved participation strengthened labor evidence. Annual wage growth slowed, while earlier construction spending showed investment remained concentrated.

section_summaries.section_title: Senegal's downgrade puts the creditor perimeter back in focus
section_summaries.summary: Senegal's downgrade raised questions about domestic claims and regional lenders. Indonesian payment problems compete for public and bank resources; Brazil's targets still lack a complete financing plan.

section_summaries.section_title: Inflation gives some central banks room to ease, others reason to wait
section_summaries.summary: Kazakhstan cut despite limited remaining room, while Czech and New Zealand pricing diverged from measured guidance. Aviva bought gilts; restrictive starting rates supported selective local EM demand.

overall_summary.headline: Payroll strength lifts hike odds, but long Treasuries hold
overall_summary.session_narrative:
September hike odds rose toward 60%, yet the initial selloff faded. Employment and participation improved, while slower annual pay growth left next week's inflation data decisive. Ten-year breakevens held at 2.35%.

Credit remained open but selective. Technology bonds offered stronger relative value, Norway proposed less government debt, and SoftBank completed a large household-targeted sale. Treasury liquidity remained weaker than other markets.

Air Baltic's proposed 25% bridge would change creditor priority. Senegal's late downgrade questioned whether domestic debt could stay excluded. Weekend tanker attacks and Chinese recapitalization plans arrived after the US close and belong to the coming Asian week's outlook.
overall_summary.summary: Payrolls rose 162,000 and revisions erased July's decline. The 2-year yield rose 3 basis points to 4.37%, but the 30-year fell 1 to 5.24% as annual wage growth slowed to 3.1%.
